threads.body: [Testing] This HTTP/1.1 fallback branch is not exercised: the new suite enables `useHttp2()`, while the existing HTTP/1.1 suite binds with HTTP/2 disabled. Because restoring the current context for HTTP/1.1 requests on an HTTP/2-enabled binding is the reported regression, add a test that sends an `h1c://` request to `PekkoHttpTestHttp2WebServer` and verifies the handler child span shares the server trace without creating a duplicate server span.
[Naming] A used `Throwable` catch variable must be named `t` under the repository's catch-variable convention; rename this variable and its uses.
[Style] Javaagent implementation classes should not be declared `final`; remove this modifier per the repository's Java style rule for `javaagent/src/main`.

[Testing] The new `h2c://` suite exercises prior-knowledge HTTP/2, so it never enters this upgrade-replay branch. Add an actual HTTP/1.1-to-h2c upgrade test that verifies the replayed request gets one new span rather than reusing or duplicating the completed upgrade-request span.
[Style] Static factory entry points belong immediately above constructors. Move `wrap` above the private constructor so construction-related members follow the repository's class-organization rule.

[Testing] Using an explicit `h2c://` URI prevents this test from exercising HTTP/1.1 upgrade: Armeria always uses the HTTP/2 connection preface when the selected session protocol is H2C, regardless of `useHttp2Preface(false)`. The request therefore still takes the prior-knowledge path and leaves the upgrade-replay branch untested. Use an `http://` URI while retaining `useHttp2Preface(false)` so upgrade is attempted first.

replies.body:
You are right, and thanks, this was a real gap. Armeria uses the preface when the uri names h2c, so the test took the prior knowledge path and the branch stayed untested. Switching to an `http://` uri while keeping `useHttp2Preface(false)` makes it negotiate, and a debug print in the wrapper confirms the branch is now reached:

```
handler path= protocol=HTTP/1.1 tracedAttr=true streamId=true upgrade=true
```

That is the replayed request: parsed by the http/1.1 engine, so it carries the attribute that `PekkoHttpServerTracer` attached, and replayed through the http/2 stack, so it also has the stream id.

Two things fell out of making it upgrade for real:

Armeria upgrades with an `OPTIONS *` request, and the handler that the other tests share only answers `GET`, so the replay hit a `MatchError` that killed the connection. The http/2 test server now answers anything that is not a `GET` with 404.

The upgrade produces three traces, not the two I expected: the http/1.1 exchange ending with 101, the replayed request with a span of its own, and the request over the upgraded connection with its controller child. The test asserts all three.

I also checked that the test fails without the branch: with `isHttp2` forced to false, `testHttp2Upgrade` fails, and it passes with the branch in place, so the coverage is real rather than incidental. That also corrects something I wrote earlier in this PR: the 101 response does get a span, my note that it did not came from the `h2c://` version of the test, where no upgrade ever happened.
